question: A form of worship in ancient and medieval India, often associated with the Goddess, in which practitioners often ignored caste and class distinctions in the ritual context, was known as _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tantrik**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tantrik** worship, in ancient and medieval India, often focused on the worship of deities, particularly **Goddesses**, and was characterized by rituals that sometimes bypassed the traditional caste and class distinctions.
 
• It **involved esoteric practices, mantras, rituals, and meditative techniques that aimed to achieve spiritual power and liberation.**
 
• Tantrism was closely linked with **Shaktism**, the worship of the feminine divine, and was seen as a form of devotion where societal norms like caste were less emphasized in the ritual context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shaiva:**

 
 
• Refers to worship centered around Shiva and was more structured with caste considerations in its practices.
 
 
 
• **Mantric:**
 
 
• While mantras (sacred chants) are an integral part of many forms of worship, including Tantrik worship, mantric rituals do not specifically highlight the disregard for caste and class distinctions as seen in Tantrism.
